surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Cates scores with 31 seconds left to lift the Flyers
paras: Christian Dvorak opened the scoring for the Flyers midway through the first, but Oliver Kapanen tied it 1-1 for Montréal just 16 seconds later. Denver Barkey and Rasmus Ristolainen scored a little over four minutes apart early in the second to put the Flyers up 3-1. Zachary Bolduc pulled the Canadiens within one on the power play early in the third. Owen Beck tied it 3-3 a little over a minute later, but that was the last goal the Habs would get. Noah Cates put the Flyers ahead for good with 31 seconds left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Dan Vladař made 20 saves for the Flyers, and Jacob Fowler stopped 16 of 20 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Arber Xhekaj had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Flyers improved to 9-11-6, fifth in the Metropolitan, while the Canadiens dropped to 14-6-4, slipping to third in the Atlantic.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Flyers.
Travis Konecny extended his point streak against Montréal to six games.
The Flyers have beaten the Canadiens four straight times, going back to last season.
Neither of the preview’s calls held.
